notes: Read all 31 numbered source lines before editing. Covered: the doc-comment intent (L1-11) explaining TeslaFeatureFlagsPage is a dedicated page wrapper that promotes the Tesla account Feature Flags surface from an inline /settings section to a first-class Integrations page whose actual UI lives in the shared <FeatureToggles /> component; the imports (L13-16) useTranslation/PageContainer/usePageTitle/FeatureToggles; and the component body (L18-31).

Component body coverage: `useTranslation('settings')` (L19) -> a native key/English-default `t` (react-i18next is not wired on native) preserving the 'settings' namespace keys verbatim; `const title = t('featureConfig.title','Feature Flags')` (L20) -> identical; `usePageTitle(title)` (L21) drives document.title which has no RN analogue, so the translated title is surfaced as the on-screen accessibilityRole="header" page header (FeatureFlagsPage precedent); the `<PageContainer title={title} subtitle={t('featureConfig.subtitle','Tesla account feature configuration')}>` (L24-27) -> an inline page scaffold (ScrollView + header title/subtitle) because PageContainer is not in the native manifest; `<FeatureToggles />` (L28) -> the inlined FeatureTogglesView; closing default export (L18,L30-31) preserved.

Inlined the web FeatureToggles component (web/src/features/settings/components/FeatureToggles.tsx) directly into this page — exactly as the sibling FeatureFlagsPage port inlined its sub-components — because FeatureToggles is NOT part of the native conversion manifest and the page renders nothing else. Ported verbatim-by-behaviour: the useTeslaFeatureConfig()/useRefreshTeslaFeatureConfig() bindings (reusing the unchanged native useUser hooks: GET /tesla/user/feature-config, POST /tesla/user/feature-config/refresh); the featureEntries useMemo (for each [key,value]: enabled = value.enabled when value is a non-null object else value, Boolean-coerced; details = the non-`enabled` entries joined as `k: JSON.stringify(v)`, or null for primitives) reproduced exactly in buildFeatureEntries; `featureConfig?.data` / `featureConfig?.fetched_at` reads; the header title/subtitle, the optional 'Synced <when>' stamp, the secondary Refresh button (disabled + spinning while pending), the Feature/Status/Details table of Badge rows, and the no-data EmptyState.

Preserved every identifier, state, API path, and i18n contract: the featureConfig/featureConfigRefresh names; featureConfig?.data / featureConfig?.fetched_at; featureConfigRefresh.isPending; the t(key, defaultString) keys kept verbatim — featureConfig.title/subtitle/lastSynced/refresh/feature/status/details/enabled/disabled/noData. The refresh mutation's toasts are handled INSIDE the unchanged native useRefreshTeslaFeatureConfig hook (onSuccess/onError already call useMutationToast with the same English 'Feature config refreshed' / 'Failed to refresh feature config' messages the web page passed), so the page calls featureConfigRefresh.mutate() WITHOUT re-passing onSuccess/onError — re-passing would double-fire the toast. The web settings-namespace toast keys (toast.featureConfigRefreshed/toast.featureConfigFailed) map to the hook's toast.user.featureConfig.success/error keys with identical user-visible English text.

DOM/web-UI swaps — no DOM, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, lucide-react, or old web UI imports: useTranslation -> native key/default `t`; usePageTitle -> on-screen header; PageContainer -> inline ScrollView scaffold (the web page passes no loading prop, so children always render, reproduced exactly); FadeIn (framer-motion) -> plain View; GlassPanel -> native GlassPanel; IconBox color="purple" + lucide Flag -> SemanticIcon name="flag"; the web Button variant="secondary" size="sm" with the spinning RefreshCw icon -> a native Pressable RefreshButton (↻ glyph; ActivityIndicator while pending; disabled while pending); formatDateTime(@/lib/dateFormat) -> an inlined absolute formatter (year/month/day + 2-digit hour:minute via toLocaleString, '—' on nullish/NaN); the Tailwind grid-cols-[1fr_auto_2fr] table -> a Feature/Status/Details header row + per-feature rows; Badge variant success/neutral -> a StatusBadge (successSurface/success vs surfaceRaised/textSecondary) showing Enabled/Disabled; EmptyState(lucide Info + message) -> an inline info block (SemanticIcon name="info" + the noData message) because the native shared EmptyState requires a title the web variant does not supply; the cn()/animate-spin and text-[var(--text-*)] Tailwind colours map to theme tokens (textPrimary/textSecondary/textMuted/success). testIDs cover every slot: tesla-feature-flags-page, tesla-feature-config-panel, tesla-feature-config-refresh, tesla-feature-config-synced, tesla-feature-config-table, tesla-feature-row-<key>, tesla-feature-status-<key>, tesla-feature-config-empty.

Gates: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint -- --quiet`, and `npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles` all pass. A root __tests__/TeslaFeatureFlagsPageParity.test.tsx mocks useTeslaFeatureConfig + useRefreshTeslaFeatureConfig and asserts: the page header + subtitle + panel + Refresh action render; the no-data empty state ('No feature config data yet. Click Refresh to fetch from Tesla.') with the synced stamp hidden; a row per feature with the Enabled/Disabled status badge, the joined object details ('tier: "beta"'), and the Feature/Status/Details column headers; the 'Synced' stamp appears when fetched_at is present; and the Refresh button shows an ActivityIndicator while the mutation isPending.
